w: Swamishri performed the pratishtha of murtis for the Hari mandir in Beraja village. Thereafter, Swamishri celebrated the symbolic 33 rd patotsav (inauguration anniversary) of the mandir and blessed the assembly.

At 9.30 a.m. Swamishri arrived at the BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir in Luton to perform the murti-pratishtha rituals. With the commencement of Vedic rituals Swamishri performed the pratishtha of Shri Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Shri Radha Krishna Dev, Guru Parampara, Shri Hanumanji and Shri Ganapatiji. After the annakut was arranged, Swamishri performed the pratishtha arti. During the pratishtha assembly Viveksagar Swami explained the importance of mandirs in society. Then Lord Navnit Dholakiya, president of the Liberal Democratic Party, addressed the assembly, “By giving over 500 mandirs to us Swamishri has given us our religion. Today we find that because of religion there are wars and killings, whereas in our Hindu mandirs we hear the words Om Shantihi, Shantihi, Shantihi.” The Mayor of Luton Councillor Michael Dolling said, “This is an occasion that I shall treasure for the rest of my life. You do Luton a very great service by establishing a mandir in our town. The Hindus of the town are a very valuable asset and contribute greatly to the cultural and social life of the area. “Your work throughout the rest of the world is well known providing spiritual and social care for millions of people. Your residential homes for the elderly, your fundraising for natural disasters such as famines or earthquakes is without equal. Not only that, you run anti-addiction drives and build hospitals and shelters in poorer countries. This work is on top of making young people aware of their social responsibilities together with training, education and good parenting skills.” Finally Swamishri blessed the assembly, “Through this mandir people will be blessed with good impressions (sanskars). Mandir is a place that stills the mind, because God is still; and one who is still can give stillness to others. The world is unstable. God is stable so He controls and keeps countless universes stable. The mandir is a place that stills the mind because by offering devotion to God, praying to Him, seeing Him and listening to His glory one is blessed with divine virtues.” The pratishtha assembly was attended by 1500 devotees.
Getting to know people is a special trait of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. It takes Swamishri no time at all to make a person his own, and that too without any flash of art, skill or intellect.
A spiritual seeker came for Swamishri's darshan. His name was Bijal Kiritbhai. As soon as he arrived, Swamishri asked, "Where are you originally from in India?"
"Nadiad."
"Is that so, which part of Nadiad?"

"Kakarkhad." On hearing this, Swamishri said, "Vad, khad and vago (the kinds of neighbourhoods). Kakarkhad has a higher status. First comes Kakarkhad, then Desaivago and then Lakhavad." Swamishri said just this much, and Swamishri's loving personality settled in Bijalbhai's heart. There was no special flourish, yet he exclaimed, "Bapa! You know the vads, khads and vagos of Nadiad. Thank you, thank you."
Even through such a simple conversation, he left feeling grateful. This is Swamishri's natural way of making contact.

Dushyant Sharma, a representative of the Queen in London, came today for the darshan of Pramukh Swami Maharaj. Referring to part of a speech given by Lord Dholakia, he said, "Dholakia said that you are a citizen of London; but not only of London, you are a citizen of Luton too."
As he was leaving, Yogesh Chag said, "Swami! Only today did we learn that you are a UK citizen."

Narrowing his eyes a little, Swamishri said, "Your vision is only that much, so you see only that much! Otherwise, if we look from the point of view of Akshardham, what is all this at all? God is everywhere. We are citizens of the whole world. Why have a narrow view? We are citizens of the whole world."
Truly, for Swamishri "the three worlds are one's own country". Swamishri belongs to everyone. Everyone can find a place in Swamishri's heart.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj seemed to be enjoying the fragrance of these divine flowers that he himself had made bloom!

In the morning, Pramukh Swami Maharaj travelled to Luton to perform the Murti Pratishtha vidhi (image installation ceremony) at the new BAPS Swaminarayan Mandir. Swamishri consecrated the murtis of Akshar Purushottam Maharaj, Radha Krishna Dev, Guru Parampara, Ganapati and Hanumanji.

Hindu worshippers throughout Luton and the surrounding Bedfordshire area were delighted that they will now be able to gather at the newly-opened mandir to practise their faith and participate in colourful festivals and celebrations that will promote strong moral and spiritual values.

The committed volunteers had prepared an annakut of 250 various vegetarian items. Other volunteers had spent months leading up to the opening, dedicating their time and immense enthusiasm to ensure that the mandir was ready in time for the grand opening.

Various dignitaries also attended the ceremony. Councillor Michael Dolling, Mayor of Luton remarked; “The city of Luton is delighted to welcome the mandir and its worshippers.” President of the Liberal Democrats, Lord Dholakia said, “I am very proud of the fantastic contribution towards social upliftment, tolerance and understanding that BAPS has made.”
In his blessings, Swamishri emphasised the importance of regular attendance at the mandir in order to achieve spiritual and personal progress.

During Swamishri’s ten-day stay in Nairobi his breakfast, lunch and dinner times were scheduled for satsang reports and presentations by children, teenagers and devotees from various towns and cities of Kenya, South Africa and Botswana. Children and teenagers recited Vachanamruts, Swamini Vato, kirtans and narrated incidents. The devotees were from Nairobi, Nakuru, Eldoret, Kisumu, Kericho, Kakamega, Thika, Durban and Lenasia (S.Africa) In the morning katha Atmatrupt Swami narrated and elaborated upon Swamishri’s incidents from the ‘Brahmopanishad’. The evening assembly agenda included a speech by Viveksagar Swami on the BAPS centenary saga, dramas and folk dances by children and teenagers from different centres and speeches by senior sadhus. Then Swamishri concluded the assembly with his blessings. Today, in the evening assembly Anandswarup Swami addressed the congregation. Swamishri arrived at 6.50 pm and children of Eldoret and Nakuru Mandals performed traditional dances. Thereafter the youths of Nairobi Mandal presented a drama entitled 'Mokshanu Dwar' drama. Finally Swamishri blessed the assembly, elaborating upon the meaning of moksha.
The weather was pleasant. Pramukh Swami Maharaj had put a cap on his head. A satsangi said to Swamishri, "Bapa! You look very handsome!"
Swamishri looked at him for a moment. He began to smile gently and said, "Only God is handsome. We are only His servants."
To Swamishri, whatever goodness there is, small or large, belongs to God.

A devotee came. Lines of distress and gloom could clearly be seen on the face of this elderly devotee. His speech too was unclear. He believed that his daughter's in-laws had killed her. Because of this he was troubled.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj said, "It is natural to be troubled, but accept that it must have been God's will. Grieving causes pain to her soul too, and if we keep enmity in our mind, we stay troubled. So do not keep enmity in your mind, because what has gone does not come back. Keeping distress achieves nothing. So accept God's will and do His bhajan and prayer."

In today's assembly the children presented various programmes. The central theme was "We have blossomed as fragrant flowers in Swami's garden." How firm even small children become in the company of Swamishri! Some such incidents were presented in today's assembly.

Speaking of what kind of children are prepared in the children's assembly, Dr Jitendrasinh Parmar said, "Once a boy named Hari came to my hospital because of an accident. He was travelling in a rickshaw and the rickshaw overturned. Because of this his condition was serious. He was brought to my hospital at 8:00 at night, so I immediately started treatment. When Hari regained consciousness ten hours later, he had to be given medicine. So I said, 'Take the medicine.' Then, even in such a condition, he said, 'I will take water and medicine only after doing my puja.' Hearing this, I too was left speechless. I tried to persuade him, yet he would not budge."

Telling an incident of his daughter Devanshi, Dipakbhai said, "My daughter Devanshi has many physical problems. Her main illness is diabetes, and she has many other illnesses. There is no permanent medicine for diabetes. So we showed her to a vaidya (Ayurvedic doctor). The vaidya asked my daughter, 'Will it be all right if the medicine contains garlic?' As a father, I too wavered for a moment, but my daughter immediately said, 'Garlic will not do at all. If the illness is to be cured, let it be cured, but onion and garlic cannot be eaten at all. Even if I die, it does not matter.'"

A volunteer named Mehulbhai, telling another inspiring incident, said, "In the Maninagar Isanpur area there is a Sindhi family that is satsangi. A girl from that family comes regularly to our girls' assembly. One day, as she was coming back from tuition on her bicycle, a cow knocked into her. This girl, named Chandni, fell down and was dragged for quite a distance. She had to be taken to the clinic immediately. She was bleeding a lot from her body. Stitches had to be put in. When the girls' volunteers got there, they saw that the stitches were being put in without anaesthetic. Yet not a single groan of pain came from this girl's lips. She was constantly chanting 'Maharaj Swami... Maharaj Swami'."

Through this children's activity, good reading habits and the spirit of austerity and vows also blossom. Many such incidents were also presented. Seeing such firmness in niyam and dharma in the small children of the BAPS Swaminarayan Sanstha, Swamishri was very pleased.

Today, because of poor health, Mahant Swami Maharaj did his puja in his own room. After the puja was over, Viveksagardas Swami asked, "Well, Swami! How did it go?"
Swamishri said joyfully, "I did 150 dandvats in a dream!"
Because of his health, Swamishri cannot do as many dandvats as he wishes at present, and his words carried the feeling that he was making up for it in his dream.
Viveksagardas Swami laughed and said, "That is it, you can do as many dandvats as you want that way!"
Everyone laughed.
In all history, who would have done dandvats in a dream? And that too counting them, 150?
Truly, with each incident he proves greater and greater.
